iut_type: Registered model name/number requirement -- whether it must exactly match the final store-sold product, how SIG actually verifies this, and the placeholder-name workaround when the final model name isn't yet finalized
customer_question: When proceeding with Bluetooth certification, is the actual store-sold product model number required as part of the product information entered at registration? If so, does that registered model number need to exactly match the model number actually sold in stores?
question_variants: How does Bluetooth SIG actually verify whether a registered model name matches what's sold in the market?
If our final product model name/number isn't decided yet, can we still register under a placeholder name?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to register for Bluetooth certification before their final product model name/number had been finalized, and needed to know whether SIG's registration requirement that the model name match the actual sold product was strictly enforced, and what would happen if a placeholder name were used instead.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth Logo certification registration requires entering the 'model name initially planned to be sold' at registration time. Bluetooth SIG's actual enforcement mechanism for verifying this works by searching: SIG monitors devices found on the market, web product-introduction pages, e-commerce listings, and tips submitted through its own website's unregistered-product reporting link, then checks whether the discovered model name and selling company name return a match via the Bluetooth product registration site's own search function. If no match is found, SIG issues a corrective recommendation to the selling company and, if necessary, conducts an audit. Critically, this means SIG's verification process can only detect a PROBLEM (an unregistered product found on the market with no matching registration) -- it has no mechanism to prove the ABSENCE of a problem, i.e., it cannot verify or disprove that there's no sales history for an already-registered model name. Some models are also sold direct-to-consumer through channels that wouldn't surface in SIG's market-monitoring search at all. While SIG's stated requirement is that the registered model number must match what's actually sold in stores, in practice, the consultant's company has registered several past clients' products under placeholder names like 'Prototype' or 'Evaluation Model' when the customer wanted to register before finalizing the actual production model name/number, and this has never caused any actual problem.
consultant_answer: Bluetooth Logo certification registration requires entering the model name initially planned to be sold. SIG verifies compliance by searching for products found on the market or via reported tips, then checking whether the model name and selling company name return a match in their registration site's search -- if not, they issue a corrective recommendation. This means SIG can detect an unregistered product, but has no way to verify the absence of sales for an already-registered model name. While the formal requirement is that the registered model number match what's actually sold, we've registered several past clients under placeholder names like 'Prototype' or 'Evaluation Model' when the final model name wasn't yet decided, without any issue arising. Important related point: if one certified model is actually sold as multiple distinct SKUs (e.g., the same product packaged as a 1-piece and a 2-piece variant, each with its own iOS/Android model number), having the certified name not match those SKUs IS technically a rules violation -- but it's fully resolved by registering every actually-sold SKU as a free derivative-product addition to the Product List. As long as every real, marketed model number returns a match when searched against the registered company name, no corrective recommendation arises at all; conversely, having an extra registered name that's never actually sold causes no problem either (and can be deleted on request if desired). If a corrective recommendation is ever issued because a sold derivative SKU wasn't yet added to the Product List, simply performing that free derivative addition registration counts as complying with the recommendation and closes out the matter.
decision_logic: When a customer needs to register before finalizing their actual production model name/number, explain that while SIG's formal requirement is an exact match to the eventually-sold product, SIG's enforcement mechanism is search-based and cannot verify a registered model's actual sales history -- and that registering under a placeholder name (e.g., 'Prototype' or 'Evaluation Model') has a track record of causing no issues in practice, while being transparent that this is a practical accommodation rather than the literal letter of SIG's stated requirement.
final_recommendation: When a customer's final product model name isn't yet decided but they need or want to register early, offer the placeholder-name approach as a practically-proven option while being clear about how it differs from SIG's literal stated requirement, so the customer can make an informed choice.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer unaware that placeholder-name registration is a practical workaround (rather than strict compliance) might either avoid registering early when there was no need to wait, or could face confusion later if asked to reconcile a placeholder-named registration against an eventual different production model name.
